findings.title: Four-field inheritance: exact test is `??` on the raw single-element array read — presence, not blankness
Event page: inline pencil-edit fields for the four inherited fields exist; no series-picker surface exists yet
findings.detail:
src/routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte (HEAD) renders each of the four inheriting fields as an independent inline pencil-edit control, in this order: event_type (~2225-2282), name (~2285-2360, testids `event-edit-input-name`/`event-detail-name`), start_datetime+duration (~2370-2545, testids include `event-edit-input-duration_minutes`, `event-detail-duration`), location (~2548-2600, `event-edit-input-location`/`event-detail-location`), description (~2603-2645, `event-edit-input-description`/`event-detail-description`). Each field's shown value is `detail.<field>` — the ALREADY-MERGED (event-or-series) value, per `isUnchanged`'s doc at +page.svelte:2050-2058 ('Note before is the DISPLAYED value, which for name/duration_minutes/location/description may be INHERITED from the parent event_series').

`grep -n -i "series"` over the whole 3233-line file returns ONLY comments (doc-only references at lines 795, 2002-2054) — there is no series-select element, no series name/label rendered anywhere, and no existing attach point. The picker described in #304 (`data-testid="event-series-select"`) has to be newly added; nothing currently displays which series (if any) an event belongs to on this page — only the merged field VALUES are shown, never the series identity itself. The natural attachment point, given the field ordering and the issue's requirement to show inheritance under the select, is near the top of the header block (before or alongside the name field, since name is the field #132 series-children most depend on) — this is a placement judgement, not verified against any existing convention [speculative].

findings.title: Event `_parent` holds season AND series together — no direct precedent for a two-typed multi-valued `_parent`, but two adjacent precedents compose correctly
findings.detail:
Verified at HEAD: an event's `_parent` array carries multiple refs distinguished only by `entity_type` (season vs event_series) — eventDetail.ts:199-201, entuSeasons.ts:145-146, seasonManage.ts:66-68 all do `(_parent ?? []).find(p => p.entity_type === 'event_series')`. This is the SAME shape as `member._parent` (org + sections, distinguished by entity_type — rosterData.ts:48-69) — NOT the same shape as `section._parent` (always exactly one value).

Two existing functions in src/lib/sections/sectionActions.ts are the applicable precedents, and neither alone is safe to reuse verbatim for events:

1. `unassignMemberSection` (sectionActions.ts:265-296) — the UNASSIGN pattern to reuse: `GET entity/{id}?props=_parent` → filter `matches = _parent.filter(p => p.entity_type === 'section' && p.reference === sectionId)` → `DELETE /property/{_id}` for every match; throws (`SectionMembershipMissingError`) if zero matches (stale state). For events this becomes: filter on `entity_type === 'event_series'` (reference match not even required, since an event can have at most one series parent) → DELETE that value's `_id`. This is exactly the UNASSIGN wire shape #304 needs, and is a verified working precedent.

2. `reparentSection` (sectionActions.ts:542-582) — the REASSIGN/atomic-overwrite pattern, BUT it hard-refuses unless `_parent` holds EXACTLY ONE value total (`existing.length !== 1` throws `SectionParentDamagedError`, line 566-568) — because a section's `_parent` is ALWAYS single-purpose. Applying `reparentSection` (or the generic `replaceEntityProperty` in src/lib/entu/replaceProperty.ts, which also picks 'the FIRST existing value' under a prop name to pair with the atomic overwrite — replaceProperty.ts:70-77) directly against an event's `_parent` would be WRONG: the GET returns BOTH the season ref and the series ref under the same `_parent` prop name, and blindly pairing 'the first existing value' with the new series id risks overwriting the SEASON parent instead of the series one, since ordering is not guaranteed. `replaceEntityProperty`'s own module doc (replaceProperty.ts:1-14) is written for single-purpose props and does not anticipate a caller where one prop name holds two independently-meaningful refs.

The correct REASSIGN shape for events, composing the two verified precedents: `GET entity/{eventId}?props=_parent` → filter to the value(s) with `entity_type === 'event_series'` → if one exists, POST atomic-overwrite `[{ _id: <that value's id>, type: '_parent', reference: newSeriesId }]` (reparentSection's atomic-pairing idiom, but filtered first — never 'the first existing value' blind); if none exists (event was standalone), plain-append POST `[{ type: '_parent', reference: newSeriesId }]` with no `_id` — this exact append-with-no-prior-series-parent shape is independently verified as the 'link-event' step of `convertEventToSeries` (src/lib/events/eventConvert.ts:310-329, `body: JSON.stringify([ref('_parent', seriesId)])`), used when a standalone event is converted into a series occurrence. No single existing function does the filtered-atomic-overwrite branch for a MULTI-typed `_parent`; #304's implementation is new code composing these two verified idioms, not a reuse of an existing function as-is.

findings.title: #132 live series-name inheritance depends on the event's OWN `name` staying absent, and the season/series lookup staying keyed on `_parent[].entity_type` — the picker must touch `_parent` only, never `name`
findings.detail:
Verified: series-child events 'carry no name of their own by design' (#304's own text, confirmed by mechanism) — `createEvent`/season creation (src/lib/entity/entityCreate.ts) omits `name` for series-generated occurrences, and `eventConvert.ts`'s step 4 ('delete-name', ~line 335+ per module comment 'deleting the event's own name value... is what makes the read-side series-name merge... take over') explicitly DELETEs the event's own name property so the merge can supply the series' name. The read-time merge that depends on this absence is duplicated in two places: `entuSeasons.ts` `listEvents` (name/duration/location merge at ~lines 155-175, series found via `_parent[].entity_type === 'event_series'` at line 145-146) and `eventDetail.ts` (lines 199-215, same `_parent[].entity_type` lookup and `??` merge).

What the picker must NOT break, both verified from the mechanism: (a) it must never write to the event's `name`/`duration_minutes`/`location`/`description` properties as a side effect of a series change — issue #304 explicitly bans copying inherited values onto the event ('Do not silently copy the series' values onto the event'), and doing so would also match the exact anti-pattern `draftWireValue`'s doc warns about (permanently masking inheritance, +page.svelte:1992-2015); (b) any REASSIGN/UNASSIGN write must touch ONLY the `_parent` value whose `entity_type === 'event_series'`, never the season `_parent` value that sits in the same array — since BOTH `listEvents`'s season-scoping (`_parent.reference=${seasonId}` query, entuSeasons.ts:134) and `eventDetail`'s season read (eventDetail.ts:200-201) re-derive season/series purely from that same `_parent[].entity_type` split, a wrongly-targeted DELETE/overwrite (the risk flagged in finding 3 above, if the atomic-overwrite is not filtered by entity_type first) would silently sever the event from its season — breaking season-scoped agenda listing and season-rights resolution (`seasonOwnerIds`/`seasonEditorIds`), not just the series inheritance #304 is targeting.

findings.title: (1) Season-scoped series list EXISTS and is reusable verbatim; but the event page's data contract doesn't expose the event's OWN seriesId or which fields are actually inherited
findings.detail:
`listEventSeriesForSeason(cfg, seasonId)` (src/lib/seasons/seasonManage.ts:74-101, returns `SeriesListItem[] = {id,name,eventCount}`) is exactly 'series belonging to this event's season' — already used by the agenda's event-CREATE picker at src/routes/+page.svelte:3335 (`loadEventCreateSeriesOptions`) and gated the same way (season must be chosen/known first). The event page already exposes `detail.seasonId` (eventDetail.ts return object, ~line 265), so `listEventSeriesForSeason(cfg, detail.seasonId)` is a straight call, no new query needed for the OPTIONS list.

However two things the picker needs are currently MISSING from `EventDetail` (src/lib/events/eventDetail.ts):
  - The event's own current series id. `loadEventDetail` computes `seriesId` locally at line 203 (`parents.find(p => p.entity_type === 'event_series')?.reference ?? ''`) but never puts it on the returned object (the return block lists id, name, eventType, startDatetime, durationMinutes, location, description, conductorIds, conductorNames, capacity, ownerIds, editorIds, seasonId, seasonOwnerIds, seasonEditorIds — no seriesId). Compare `seasonId`, which IS carried for exactly this reason (comment: '`seasonId` is part of the returned contract now'). The picker's 'current series preselected' requirement needs this added.
  - Whether each of the four fields is the event's OWN value or the series fallback. eventDetail.ts:210-215 collapses `event.name ?? series.name ?? ''` etc. into one merged value; the raw event-only value is discarded. #304's requirement 'list only the fields actually inherited by this event' cannot be computed from the current `EventDetail` shape — it needs either the raw own-values (nullable) or an explicit isInherited flag per field, an extension to the data layer, not just a UI addition.

A write path to actually change the event's `_parent` series ref does not exist anywhere in the codebase yet (grep for a series-reassign/set function came up empty in src/lib) — this is new backend work, not just UI wiring for the picker's mutation half.

findings.title: (2) The reusable confirm/armed-pair idiom: #203's delete trigger→confirm/cancel on this same page, quoted verbatim
findings.detail:
src/routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte:215-222 (state) and :555-610 (arm/cancel/confirm functions) and :3163-3225 (template) is the precedent to reuse:
  - State: `deleteArmed` (bool) swaps the idle trigger for a confirm/cancel pair, writes nothing; `deletePending` disables both buttons during the one write in-flight; `deleteError` set only on a REJECTED confirm, never cleared by arming/cancelling.
  - `armDelete()`: sets armed=true, `await tick()`, then focuses the confirm button (WCAG 2.4.3 — each flip unmounts the button that held focus, so focus is placed explicitly).
  - `cancelDelete()`: armed=false, error=null, `await tick()`, focus returns to the trigger. Nothing is called — 'writes nothing'.
  - `confirmDelete()`: the only path that actually mutates; on failure keeps `armed=true` (pair stays mounted, retry/cancel still one tap away) and sets a discriminated `deleteError`.
  - Template: the armed pair REPLACES the trigger (never coexist), confirm/cancel are both `disabled={pending}` `aria-busy` where relevant, and the whole block sits behind an `isEditor` gate at the FOOT of the page with a visible, non-icon-only label (per the #237 stated choice) — review note F2 explains why: mid-page a bare glyph reads as a 5th field affordance, so this control needs a NAMED, low-in-tab-order location.
  A second, lighter-weight instance of the same idiom exists for per-row removal: `scheduleRemoveArmedId` (:286-287, :1386-1397, :2801-2818) — one row armed at a time via a nullable id rather than a boolean, useful if the picker's confirm ends up living inline next to the select rather than in its own danger-zone block.
  Both are explicitly commented as following 'the SAME two-step confirm shape as the agenda's #197 season-manage delete rows' — so this idiom is already the third instance in the codebase, not a one-off.

findings.title: (3) #304's #233 section overstates what #233's design of record actually commits to — the series-name-in-formula piece is an unadopted 'nice-to-have', not settled
findings.detail:
Read #233 in full (body + all 5 comments) and compared against #304's #233 paragraph. #304 says: '#233 moves the app's event name off `name` and onto a new `event_name`, with `name` becoming a formula that includes the parent series' name (confirmed to resolve).'

#233's actual design of record (§A.2, Mihkel's verbatim commission, and the body's own 'Design of record' quote: "'name' field becomes formula of all three values -- date, type, name") specifies the entu-side formula as exactly THREE inputs: date-part of `start_datetime`, `event_type`, `event_name`. There is no series-name component in the committed spec. Q4 in #233's own body explicitly frames series-name inclusion as 'Nice-to-have, not required by this spec' contingent on feasibility. Pérotin's Q4 answer (comment 5) confirms it is TECHNICALLY POSSIBLE (`_parent.event_series.name` resolves cleanly via formula.js:398-431) but nowhere does any comment or the body's §A.2/Done-when adopt it — Q4 answers feasibility, not a ruling to use it. #233 is still OPEN with no comment electing to widen the formula past 3 fields.

So #304's parenthetical '(confirmed to resolve)' conflates 'confirmed feasible if wanted' with 'confirmed adopted.' Concretely, this affects #304's next sentence too: '...and reassignment would additionally re-derive the entu listing name, which is the intended effect' — under the literal 3-field design of record, reassigning an event's series does NOT touch `start_datetime`, `event_type`, or `event_name`, so the entu `name` formula's output is UNCHANGED by a series reassignment; the 're-derive the listing name' effect only exists if the unadopted series-name nice-to-have is separately picked up. This is worth flagging back to Gama before implementation proceeds on that assumption — either #233 needs the Q4 nice-to-have explicitly ruled in, or #304's stated 'intended effect' for reassignment doesn't hold under the current #233 spec.

On the part #304 gets right: the app-side READ merge description is accurate to #233 §B — #233 explicitly lists `eventDetail.ts:210` as a read site to move from `event.name ?? series.name` to `event.event_name ?? series.name`, same fallback shape, and #233 explicitly scopes its formula change to the EVENT type only ('name on season / event_series / ... is untouched') — so `series.name` itself is a plain string field, unaffected by #233 regardless of landing order. This matters for ordering: if #304 lands first, whatever it builds to preview 'what the fields will become' reads `series?.name` (untouched by #233) and reads the EVENT's own `name` (which DOES move to `event_name` if #233 lands second) — so the concrete site #233's implementer would need to add to its §B enumeration, if #304 ships first, is wherever the picker reads the event's OWN name value to decide 'is this field inherited' (since that's a NEW read of `event.name`/`event.event_name` outside the existing enumerated eventDetail.ts:210 merge). Also worth noting: per finding (1) above, the actual WRITE the picker performs is a `_parent` series-ref swap only — it does not write `name`/`event_name`/`duration_minutes`/etc at all (per #304's own 'inherited values are not copied' non-goal) — so #233's WRITES enumeration (§B, entityCreate.ts/eventFieldEdit.ts/eventConvert.ts) is unaffected by #304 either way.

findings.title: (4) Event-page spec enumeration; the direct series-inheritance-merge tests use toMatchObject (safe for additive contract changes) and DOM assertions are scoped by data-testid (low collision risk)
findings.detail:
Full spec enumeration for `src/routes/event/[id]/`:
  - page.spec.ts (2515 lines) — the big one; contains `describe('loadEventDetail — series inheritance (read-time merge, verbatim listEvents semantics)')` at line 322, three tests asserting the name/duration/location/description merge directly against `loadEventDetail`'s output, PLUS a description-hidden-when-both-absent test (~507) and a duration-absent test (~615). All three inheritance tests use `expect(detail).toMatchObject({...})` (partial), not `toEqual` — so adding `seriesId` or own-value/isInherited fields to `EventDetail`'s return shape will NOT break these tests; they'd only need editing if the MERGE semantics for name/duration/location/description themselves change (they don't, per #304 — the picker changes the series ref, not the merge formula).
  - page.event-editing.spec.ts (1413 lines), page.event-type-edit.spec.ts (689), page.location-datalist.spec.ts (435) — all reference 'series' (11-22 hits each), presumably exercising the SAME inherited-value-vs-own-value distinction that the field-edit pencils already reason about (see the extensive comment block at +page.svelte:2050-2010 explaining why an idle pencil-confirm on an inherited field must not materialize the series default as a permanent override — this is pre-existing, deliberate logic that #304's 'do not silently copy' non-goal is consistent with, not introducing a new invariant).
  - page.event-delete.spec.ts (431, 8 series hits), page.schedule.spec.ts (1269, 7 hits), page.i18n-a11y.spec.ts (921, 9 hits) — lighter touches, likely fixture-only.
  - page.session-expired.spec.ts (156) and page.tally-deactivated.spec.ts (290) — zero series mentions, unaffected.
  DOM assertions on the merged name field (page.spec.ts lines ~453,480,514,557,576,600,622,1316,2247,2298) all query `[data-testid="event-detail-name"]` specifically and use `.textContent` `.toContain(...)` — scoped to that one element, not the whole page. As long as the new picker's inheritance note/consequence text is NOT rendered inside that same testid element (the delete-pair precedent puts its own affordance in a separate, named, testid'd container — `event-detail-danger-zone` — suggesting the same pattern here), these ~10 assertions are unaffected.
  None of the fetched specs currently exercise a series REASSIGNMENT write (no write function exists yet, per finding 1), so this would be genuinely new test surface, not a modification of existing inheritance tests.

findings.title: (5) i18n: an almost-identical picker already exists on the event-CREATE form with an established Estonian vocabulary that diverges from #304's verbatim suggested copy; and the locale-completeness guard is prefix-scoped, which constrains the new key names
findings.detail:
src/routes/+page.svelte:7493-7506 (event-create form, on the agenda page) already has a native `<select data-testid="event-create-series">` with a 'none' option and an inherited-value preview line, i18n keys (messages/en.json:473-478, mirrored in et/lv/uk):
  - `event_create_series_label`: en 'Series' / et 'Seeria' / lv 'Sērija' / uk 'Серія'
  - `event_create_series_none`: en 'No series (standalone)' / et 'Ilma seeriata' / lv 'Bez sērijas' / uk 'Без серії'
  - `event_create_inherited_from_series` ({value}): en 'From series: {value}' / et 'Seeriast: {value}' / lv 'No sērijas: {value}' / uk 'Із серії: {value}'

  #304's issue body specifies the label as *"Sari"* and the none-option as *"Ei kuulu sarja"* — both diverge from the app's existing 'seeria' vocabulary for the same concept (event_series). 'Sari' and 'seeria' are both valid Estonian for 'series' but using both for the identical entity type across two pickers on adjacent pages (agenda event-create vs. event-detail) reads as two names for one thing. Worth flagging back before implementing verbatim — this is the PO's literal wording in the issue, so it may be a deliberate restated choice, but it isn't consistent with the standing convention and nothing in #304 acknowledges the existing `event_create_series_*` keys at all.
  Also directly relevant to consequence-line copy: the create-form's per-field 'From series: {value}' preview line (rendered conditionally per field, e.g. `event-create-name-inherited` at +page.svelte:~7541) is presentation-only preview with NO confirm-armed gate (nothing is committed until form submit) — a genuinely different mechanism from #304's 'confirm before write' requirement on the detail page, so it's a naming/wording precedent, not a UI-mechanics one (mechanics precedent is the #203 delete pair, finding 2).

  Locale-completeness guard scope: `src/routes/event/[id]/page.i18n-a11y.spec.ts:349-356` only auto-checks keys prefixed `event_detail_`, `event_edit_`, or `event_type_` for presence across et/lv/uk. New keys should use one of those three prefixes (`event_detail_series_*` fits naturally and slots into the existing block at messages/en.json:358-388) to get free locale-completeness coverage; a `event_series_*` prefix (matching the issue's suggested `data-testid="event-series-select"`) would silently bypass this guard and need the guard's filter array extended.
  Separately, the WCAG 2.5.3 label-in-name guard (`page.repertoire-a11y.spec.ts:306-320`, ruled on #288) is scoped to `repertoire_*` keys only and has no equivalent instance on the event-detail page's spec at all — so whatever prefix the new keys get, no EXISTING automated guard enforces label-in-name for them on this page; #288's ruling ('a select whose default visible text is a placeholder PROMPT is in scope; a select that only ever displays a chosen VALUE stays out') is the right rule to apply manually since the series select always shows a real value ('Ei kuulu sarja'/'Seeria X'), never a placeholder prompt — so #304's claim that it stays outside the guard is correct in principle, just not automatically enforced for this page today.
